title: Alcaraz Wins Big After a Long Time Away
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz ended the tennis season with a big win. The 23-year-old from Spain beat world number one Alexander Zverev in Turin on Sunday to win his first ATP Finals title.

It was the end of a strange year for Alcaraz. In January, he won the Australian Open and became the youngest man to win all four of tennis's biggest tournaments. But then a wrist injury kept him away from the sport for four months. He missed most of the clay season and all of the grass-court season.

Alcaraz came back at the US Open 84 days ago, but he lost in the quarter-finals to Ben Shelton. Since then, he has won 21 of his last 22 matches. He has now won three tournaments in a row, and nine matches in a row against top-10 players.

Even a sore left leg could not stop him in Turin. He hurt his hamstring on Wednesday, but he still won. 'The injury made me realise what's really important,' Alcaraz said. 'It's not winning. It's just about playing tennis.'
why_it_matters: It shows that coming back after an injury takes patience, and that loving what you do matters more than always winning.
